title: Unreceived material POs are not duplicates: 30,670 of 30,888 are scrap-replacement buys placed the day scrap is reported, sized to the scrap, and never receipted
conclusion: The hypothesis does not hold. The 2016-2025 records show a fixed pattern. A job's first material PO is received, and every later PO on the job is not: all 30,670 follow-up POs are unreceived, against 218 of 76,267 first POs (q253). Each job has almost exactly as many follow-up POs as scrap reports (q235). 30,652 of 30,670 follow-ups are dated the same day as a scrap report (q237), and their pounds match scrap qty × the job's pounds per piece (median ratio 0.994, p10-p90 0.917-1.07, q239). They are small: median 43.5 lb, or 3.3% of the first PO (q233). Duplicates would look like the first PO, but only 304 of 30,888 unreceived POs are within 10% of a received PO's pounds (q228). Jobs with follow-ups shipped in full on 24,998 of 25,258 (q240), which suggests the material arrived. Interpretation: receipts are simply never entered for replacement buys. GL material equals all material PO dollars to a ratio of 1.0000 in every year (q249), so these buys are charged as material. That is correct if the material arrived: it is the real cost of scrap, $2,358,681 over 2016-2025 (q249), about $235,868/yr or 2.59% of GL material (q251). It is not an overstatement. The 218 unreceived first POs are edge effects: 132 sit on jobs carried in from before the records start, and 86 were ordered in Dec 2025 and are still open (q243, q246). Action: have receiving key receipts for replacement POs (or tag them as scrap replacement) so the 'no receipt' flag means something. Any saving lies in reducing scrap, not in recovering duplicate spend.

claims.text: Material POs follow a fixed pattern per job: the first PO is received and every later PO is not. Follow-up POs: 30,670, all unreceived. First POs: 218 unreceived of 76,267. Follow-ups go only to vendors 1, 3 and 4, never to vendor 2. That is why vendor 1 shows 44.16% unreceived and vendor 2 0.11%.

They are not duplicates. 30,652 of 30,888 unreceived POs do sit on a job with a received same-material PO, but only 304 are within 10% on pounds (38 within 1%). Follow-ups are a median 43.5 lb, 3.3% of the first PO (p90 11.6%), ordered a median 11 days later.

Follow-ups are scrap-replacement buys. Jobs with 1, 2 or 3+ follow-ups have 20,712, 7,734 and 2,240 scrap reports (20,698, 3,866 and 710 jobs). Jobs with no follow-up have 116 scrap reports across 50,993 jobs. 30,652 of 30,670 follow-ups are dated the same day as the matching scrap report. Pounds / (scrap qty × first-PO pounds per piece) has a median of 0.994 (p10 0.917, p90 1.07).

Jobs with unreceived follow-ups still completed and shipped in full: 24,998 of 25,258, against 50,643 of 50,791 jobs whose POs were all received. This points to material that arrived without a receipt record, not material that never came.

GL material equals total material PO dollars (received or not) at a ratio of 1.0000 in each year 2016-2025, so unreceived buys are expensed. Unreceived dollars equal follow-up dollars exactly in 2017-2024 ($177,011-$336,950/yr). The scrap-material memo is 1.0053-1.1624 times the follow-up dollars. Over 10 years the follow-ups total $2,358,681, an average of $235,868/yr and 2.59% of GL material.

The 218 unreceived first POs are edge effects. 117 sit on jobs created in Dec 2015 and 15 on jobs created 2016-01-01 to 01-03, all ordered in Jan 2016. 86 were ordered 2025-12-11 to 12-31. This gives the gaps between unreceived and follow-up dollars: $7,549 in 2016 and $123,166 in 2025.

not_evidence_of: That ~$236k/yr is lost or overstated: it is the material cost of scrap replacement, and the jobs shipped. It also isn't evidence that vendor 1 or receiving is failing; the vendor skew comes from where replacement buys are sent. The scrap-memo/follow-up ratio above 1 isn't explained, but it says nothing about duplicates.
could_not_tell: Whether replacement material physically arrived and was paid for: there are no vendor invoices or payments in the warehouse, and no PO status or cancellation field. Whether some replacement needs were filled from stock while the PO was left open, or cancelled: the records can't tell these apart. Why the scrap memo runs 0.5-16% above follow-up PO dollars.
next_step: Pull vendor invoices/AP for vendors 1, 3 and 4 for a sample of follow-up POs to confirm they were billed and delivered. Require receipts (or a 'scrap replacement' PO type) on replacement buys. Treat the ~$236k/yr as scrap cost and pursue it through the scrap hypotheses (by reason code and work centre).
dead_ends: Duplicate re-orders of similar pounds: only 304 of 30,888 within 10% (q228)
Vendor-specific receiving failure: the skew is fully explained by follow-ups going to vendors 1/3/4 (q253)
Unreceived POs with no other PO on the job: only 218, all at the window edges (q243, q246)
Missing material on jobs: jobs with unreceived POs shipped in full at a similar rate (q240)
